purpose: Exercise rubric interpretation. These invented responses are exposed for development and must never become reserved outcome evidence.
public_prompt: Adapt the published community-centre kiosk example. Teaching assumptions: the kiosk must issue a valid visitor pass within 15 seconds after accepting a valid sign-in; it must also record that sign-in. Record format and retention are unresolved. Write independent product obligations and a feasible verification check. Distinguish the timing result from whether visitors can reach the correct activity using the pass. Propose an observable intended-use check, clearly identifying any proposed acceptance assumptions.

responses.text: The kiosk shall issue the visitor's valid pass within 15 seconds after accepting a valid sign-in. Separately, the kiosk shall record each accepted sign-in. Record format and retention remain unresolved; the service owner will resolve them against operational needs before baseline approval at the design review. Check elapsed time from sign-in acceptance to pass issuance using video with timing resolution adequate for 15 seconds; inspect the recorded sign-in separately. A timing pass alone does not show useful navigation. Observe representative visitors, including relevant accessibility needs, using the pass to reach the correct activity in the intended setting. Proposed use criterion, subject to stakeholder agreement: the visitor reaches the intended activity without staff correcting the destination; retain failures and help.
The kiosk shall quickly issue passes and record everything. Run a test. If the machine works and people like it, it is validated.

The kiosk shall issue a valid pass within 3 seconds after accepting a valid sign-in. The kiosk shall record each accepted sign-in; format and retention need owner resolution before baseline. Check timestamp differences against 3 seconds and inspect sign-in records. Also observe representative visitors using the pass in the intended setting to reach the correct activity without destination correction, treating that use criterion as a proposal for stakeholder agreement. Timing compliance alone does not demonstrate usefulness.

The kiosk shall issue a valid pass within 15 seconds after accepting a valid sign-in. The kiosk shall record each accepted sign-in. Record format and retention require the service owner's decision before design review and baselining. Film a representative visitor completing the workflow: measure the acceptance-to-pass interval against 15 seconds and separately observe whether the pass leads them to the correct activity. Include the intended environment and relevant accessibility needs. No staff destination correction is a proposed use-success criterion to agree with stakeholders. The same trial supports two different evaluations; passing timing does not guarantee the use outcome.

The kiosk shall issue a valid pass within 15 seconds after accepting a valid sign-in. It shall separately record each accepted sign-in. Format and retention are unresolved and require service-owner agreement before the design review. Measure elapsed time with adequate resolution between acceptance and issue, and inspect a corresponding record. Once timing and recording pass, the kiosk is useful by definition.

The kiosk shall deliver seamless, human-centred check-in excellence, robust records and measurable stakeholder value. Apply holistic verification and user-focused validation with rigorous traceability, emphasizing confidence, operational success and continuous improvement.
